contracts.statement: Snapshots and replay preserve an entire same-Scope, single-version multi-key commit. This check covers controlled serial examples only; concurrent interleavings remain a separate gap.

Same-version/same-content retry adds no history; conflicting content is rejected without state change. Maximum uint64 versions retain identical replay receipts, reject conflicting content and wrapped zero, keep evicted older receipts uncertain, preserve durable state/notifications across two attempts and reopen with the complete maximum-version record.
Failure of the second SQL insert rolls back the first update, version, and history. Commit succeeds after removing the fault.
Bounded history rejects lagging cursors and retains a contiguous suffix. Normal close/reopen preserves data and versions; it does not establish power-loss durability.

Complete component-maintenance admission covers every applicable rule and the L3 coverage, independent-model, fault, mutation, and delivery matrices. Existing tests do not imply completeness on initial adoption.

Every length-three sequence over the declared nine operations agrees with an independent two-key map and retained-log model; 729 sequences, 2187 transitions, no pruning. This excludes concurrent schedules and power-loss recovery.
All eight declared mutating SQL boundaries reach the injected failure, preserve records/history/accounting, and recover after removal. Statement failures do not prove fsync or power-loss durability.

All 972 declared two-writer pairs across four initial states and three version relationships have one joint legal serial order for receipts, the final state/log, 16 concurrent snapshots and 16 concurrent replays. Retained snapshots remain unchanged. Internal schedules and power-loss recovery are not exhaustive.
Independent fixed journal examples anchor next-version commits, gaps and identical/conflicting retries; the snapshot/history predicates reject partial or mixed states.

Real SQLite begin, commit-before, commit-after/lost-receipt, commit cancellation, rollback-receipt and mid-batch cancellation reach twice across close/reopen. Complete state/history/accounting, publication and resource cleanup are checked. This excludes power loss, failed fsync and all driver-internal schedules.
A real partial transaction write followed by an application panic rolls back and releases the native transaction while preserving the original panic; later commits remain possible.

Owned child processes are killed after the first mutating SQL statement, immediately before native COMMIT, and after successful COMMIT before its receipt. Recovery preserves the complete old or committed state/history/accounting, retries publish exactly once, and later commits remain possible. This excludes power loss, failed fsync and driver-internal crash positions.

Thirty-four independently constructed SQLite corruptions are rejected at their declared read/startup boundaries, with no partial result, no repair of SQL values/schema, no contamination of the healthy scope and no retained database ownership after two rejected opens. This is logical-format corruption, not physical page damage or power loss.

Missing scopes return version zero; present versions match commits; invalid, over-capacity and closed public reads return their declared errors without partial values. Removing the injected excess scope restores the complete list without automatic repair.

Nine native SQLite authorizer refusals cover public list/version/snapshot/history preparation and startup quick-check/scope/foreign-key queries. Each refusal is reached once, yields the declared error without partial values, preserves SQL state and releases its connection; removal permits reading, writing and validation. Eight native database/sql cursor scenarios additionally verify error precedence and immediate release at EOF, after a real orphan row, during cancellation and with an explicitly different result-set-continuation capability. Native SQLite must lack that optional interface; the continuation control must make a finalization error independently observable.

Snapshot and journal queries each reach a second native row after a prefix, then fail via a SQLite function error or explicit cancellation. All six cases, including forced post-cancellation connection replacement, return unavailable without partial results, drain their transactions and recover unchanged state and subsequent writes. Connection-local views preserve the durable schema.

A pinned real read mark and a WAL over its configured threshold force incomplete checkpoint rejection for reads and writes. Native PRAGMA refusal and filesystem stat errors are distinguished from an absent WAL. Releasing the reader/removing the fault restores checkpointing and writes without changing logical state.

Five native connection setup checks reject denied checkpoint/trust assignments, a denied journal-mode query, disabled foreign keys and reduced synchronous mode, then recover after restoring the original settings. A direct native connection independently requires all four acquired pragma cursors to be finalized before Store initialization can mask a missing close. Twelve additional driver-response scenarios cover iteration, finalization and combined error receipts for each of the four queried pragmas. Each scenario rejects twice, finalizes every acquired native cursor, preserves durable contents and notifications, reconfigures the same connection after each fault and then permits a healthy commit.

Six native SQLite authorizer refusals cover current scope, metadata, old record size, retry history, history clearing and prefix selection. Every site fails twice, returns no receipt, preserves exact durable state and notifications, drains admission/connections and then recovers a complete commit.

A deletion with understated record/byte accounting and an excess retained-history counter reject with corruption, preserving the damaged input without partial writes or notifications. Restoring the independently specified baseline permits normal commits. These are two explicit damage cases, not detection of every possible database inconsistency.

Four scenario groups reject an empty batch and a truncated later entry, enforce feed count and aggregate bytes with exact idempotent release, reject FIFO/symlink/missing/duplicate lock targets, and propagate a real lock-descriptor close failure while closing SQL pools and refusing later writes. An owned Linux/amd64 child injects two native fstat EIO results, verifies immediate descriptor release, healthy reacquisition and unchanged lock inode, content and permissions. Owned Linux/amd64 children separately force native WAL write and sync EIO twice each, observe the real SQLite COMMIT error, expose no receipt or partial notification, drain descriptors and verify old-or-wholly-new durable state/history/accounting plus exactly-once retry on an unaffected recovery thread. This does not simulate power loss or storage hardware behavior.

A controlled query-result substitution returns a native integer instead of the declared version BLOB in the real SQLite transaction. The prefix scan rejects once without a receipt, preserves durable state, drains the transaction and permits later unmodified commits.

Authority Galaxy and username names contain only ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen and occupy 1..64 bytes. An independent literal alphabet checks all 256 bytes alone and at every position of a 64-byte name, the empty/64/65-byte boundaries and valid non-ASCII Unicode.

All 198 declared 64-bit representation, exact quota, native SQLite BLOB-order, guarded batch length, budget-accounting and durable high-version boundary vectors agree with independent expectations under complete ten-file production identity and five pinned Go runtime source assumptions. This named observation alone does not discharge whole-Storage numeric or other component obligations.

Ten declared numeric semantic substitutions must fail the actual TestNumeric after a passing identical baseline. Compile failure, timeout and missing output are not semantic detection; whole-Storage mutation remains separate.

The native Go compiler export boundary covers all nine active and one inactive Storage source files. All 882 typed numerical uses, comparisons, compound assignments, increments, range variables and slices bind exact bytes and 36 owning scopes; source, metadata, export or denominator drift blocks this inventory. Complete numerical and release qualification remain separate.

Twenty-three valid, independently specified numerical fixture families must be detected by the real Go type checker, while a pure string fixture must remain non-numerical. Complete affected Boolean, control-flow and source-integrity tool tests must still pass; parser/type errors do not count as sensitivity.

Twenty-seven ordered request-intent observations across retained, evicted and disabled durable receipt windows distinguish identical/nil-empty/explicit entry versions from changed bytes, keys, erase intent, order, omission and additional entries. Every attempt preserves full durable state/history/accounting, emits no duplicate notification, drains transactions and keeps old evidence after restart. Six independent Scope commits prove isolation by both hierarchy levels. Caller authentication and cross-system effects remain separate.

Three controlled native Race schedules require admitted real transactions to drain before database close, queued writer cancellation to release admission, later Commit/Load/Subscribe calls to wait behind closing and then refuse, notification/feed/pool reservations to terminate once, and reopen to retain only the permitted complete committed or rolled-back state. Runtime lock observations and reached real SQL boundaries supply scheduling evidence; this named scope does not qualify the complete lifecycle/fault matrix or containing-service shutdown.

All eight combinations of healthy/lost native read and write connection-close receipts and an actual already-closed lock descriptor must still release every later resource, terminate notifications/reservations, refuse late writes, close idempotently and reopen the previously durable state. Each SQL receipt fault occurs after a real SQLite connection closes; this bounded matrix does not prove that an arbitrary failed native close releases its handle, hardware I/O progress or full service shutdown.

Two controlled native histories require public Commit and List cancellation to retain lifecycle admission until the real database/sql background rollback finishes. An explicit connection borrow must wait at the actual pinned closingMutex boundary, then return with no pool/writer ownership and complete native close accounting. This supplements service/stop/fault obligations and does not alone qualify hardware I/O progress or the complete async rule.

Refusal before native SQL begins covers read, write and recovery-validation owners for closed pools, cancelled contexts and already expired deadlines. Closed pools retain ErrUnavailable; cancellation and expiry preserve the established context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded semantics. Every refusal leaves zero writer/connection ownership, no feed/change receipt, and the exact durable version/record after Close and reopen. These nine histories supplement lifecycle/fault acceptance and do not replace transaction-finalization or whole-component obligations.

All eight native mutating SQL sites complete two refusal/refusal/recovery cycles with the same Store, pools and subscriber: 32 reached refusals and 16 complete recovered commits, with full rollback, accounting, history, notifications and ownership checks. This supplements rather than replaces initialization, read, finalization, native I/O, cleanup and process-death fault domains.

All three configured deadline owners are exercised with native SQLite and standard-library virtual time: seven writer, seven read-pool and eight opening histories. Two native host-timer histories independently verify elapsed cancellation. Eight physical owned-source mutation controls establish sensitivity. Cancellation preserves durable state and admission ownership; opening retains its initialized file and drains I/O before releasing its lock. Durations use Go monotonic context time; Storage owns no civil-time schedule, persisted deadline, distributed lease or random generator. This does not establish a scheduler latency SLO or a hard timeout for uninterruptible native I/O.

A native SQLite online backup fixes one source read transaction containing two independent scopes at version one. Both version-two commits finish while native copying is active. The completed image preserves all known values and version one, while the live authority independently retains both acknowledged version-two writes. Ordinary and Race cases must pass; copying the main database file without its WAL must fail the recovery oracle. This finite component case does not promise that an older backup includes later writes, power-loss durability or a service-level RPO/RTO.

With writers quiesced after both version-two acknowledgements, native SQLite backup and restoration to a separate working image preserve complete known values, versions and retry receipts. Identical retries do not publish, conflicting retries fail without side effects, and both scopes accept version three. Store shutdown drains owned maintenance and SQL pools, and the retained backup bytes remain unchanged. Ordinary and Race cases must pass; substituting a valid version-one image must fail the acknowledged-watermark oracle. This finite component case does not qualify capacity, power loss, production migration or the whole release rule.

contracts.statement: Complete 18^3 sequential directory histories on two principals and two epochs at capacities one and two, using independent register maxima and explicit stale-handshake rejection. Bounds exclude cryptography, arbitrary identities and internal memory schedules.

Each pair of the 18 operations, from five starting states at capacities one and two, has a legal serial commit order including per-call outcomes and final fields. A start barrier introduces overlap; it does not enumerate internal or weak-memory schedules.
Installed and observed identity messages and returned membership snapshots have independent mutable storage; caller mutation cannot change current identity or stored fields.

Full admission maintenance qualification includes independent decision/fault/mutation denominators, cryptographic input and certificate boundaries, platform execution, and approved protected evidence. Bounded directory models do not establish the full package.
Supported roles produce one owned unopened channel and a 32-byte startup request; invalid identity, numeric endpoint, galaxy, group or role returns no Node.
Pending Nodes publish no credential context. Registered Member/Hello messages are independent copies, and context extension preserves input metadata while refusing existing admission keys.

Thirteen controlled response/transport boundaries reject twice with unchanged startup request, no partial process credentials, unchanged directory and released admission slot. A subsequent current response recovers the same Node; a ready Node does not register again. A nonempty list containing only another member cannot publish partial directory state.

Pending, failed, invalid-list, superseded-process and duplicate-context refreshes return the specified errors and retain process credentials; a healthy refresh retains current admission and releases its slot. Five source-bound refresh failure classes must each reject twice without changing credentials, directory, request identity or admission ownership. Disarmed transient faults recover on the same Node; observed process replacement remains a terminal refusal even for a later healthy older reply.

A latched real Register owns the shared slot. Cancelled competing Register/Refresh calls never enter transport or release that slot; release publishes exactly one complete identity and the worker is joined.

Nine transient receipts request the independently specified 500ms-to-30s capped delays and reuse one request before success. Permanent refusal never waits; waiting and blocked-admission cancellation terminate the loop.

Refresh waits follow the explicit 30s-to-120s capped sequence, reset after success and preserve callback order. Permanent refusal, waiting cancellation and callback cancellation stop the owned loop. An absent callback still permits a complete refresh followed by cancelled waiting, with released admission ownership.
The actual timer completes at zero duration and cancels without elapsed waiting; the explicit transient/permanent error table preserves retry classification.

Public Join and Refresh consume real generated RPCs over repository-fixture TLS, transport exact admission metadata, publish current identity and avoid repeated registration; the listener, client and serving worker are closed and joined.

Six file-boundary mutants attack stat/kind/read/close errors and omitted or duplicate handle closure; one constructor mutant attempts to publish a Node after native gRPC client creation fails. Compilation failures, timeouts and incomplete cleanup never count as killed. This finite denominator does not qualify whole-Admission mutation coverage. The additional twenty-nine security mutations require their own six unchanged named baselines and semantic rejection; the two sets are conjunctive, with separate native identities and denominators. Seven additional current acquisition mutations use byte-bound same-package test overlays on both baseline and mutant commands; all three check groups are mandatory. Legacy mutation evidence remains source-bound and is not automatically current after acquisition changes.

Directory construction accepts the three supported roles and exact 1..16384 limits; invalid arguments publish no directory. Verified capacity overflow, endpoint alias and missing metadata leave committed members unchanged and return precise refusals.

An explicit independent alphabet verifies all 256 single-byte names and length boundaries. Invalid login objects and eleven correctly signed malformed identities are rejected; maximum-length valid passwords and scalar TLS configuration copies retain their specified behavior.

Fourteen native Linux material scenarios begin from a passing public fixture. Missing/nonregular/link/unreadable/oversized material, bad keys/roots/intermediates and wrong endpoint authorization publish no Identity; a valid explicit chain loads. This is a bounded physical boundary matrix, not all stat/read/close failure injection.

Every one of five public material slots exercises lstat/nonregular/open/stat/restat/read/partial-read/close refusal twice, followed by disarmed recovery. All 120 native-backed cells retain exact inspected/opened/closed prefixes, stable refusal and no partial Identity. The complete 1501-assertion stream is independently reconciled against its frozen source. Two real NewClient refusals must preserve the exact dependency error and publish no partial Node; restoring the registry must permit a channel that closes successfully. All nine member-equality predicates have frozen actual-input opposite-result pairs. Nullable operands use short-circuit masking; seven business fields each vary independently. Source-bound interpretation rejects missing or changed pairs. This named function scope is not full Admission MC/DC.

An independent literal transition model covers both supported roles, eight Join and three refresh backoff prefixes, and all 27 three-receipt suffixes: 594 complete histories without pruning. Seven fixed axioms anchor the model; native scheduling and arbitrary cryptographic/network faults remain separate obligations.

An independent five-state, nine-operation literal table specifies pending/admitted credential publication, absent/current/newer directory identities, no replay after admission and refusal atomicity. Both supported roles execute all 1458 length-three histories, 4374 transitions and 1508 RPC receipts without pruning; seven fixed examples independently anchor the table. Controlled transport retains real signature checks and Node/Directory ownership. Native interleavings, arbitrary payloads and whole-Admission qualification remain separate obligations.

Thirty-one opposite-result input pairs cover Name length/alphabet predicates, four admitted roles, nine member-format guards, the endpoint-result decision of Valid and all six NewDirectory guards. Nil member input uses masking. Constructor pairs change one public field and one guard value and verify accepted state and stable refusal. Exact source binding and original values are required; Endpoint internals and other Admission code remain outside this named decision scope.
All thirty-one fixed predicate omissions must fail TestPredicates after a passing baseline; compiler failures, missing outcomes and survivor counts cannot be accepted as kills.

The complete pinned Linux/amd64 admission production scope uses integer byte/capacity/enum/epoch/duration semantics. Source-bound unbounded interval derivation proves reachable doubling, random-bound conversion and jitter addition fit int64; 225 native records and 1046 assertions verify widths, full uint64 ordering and exact byte/port/capacity limits. Parent acceptance additionally requires existing format, file and loop evidence.
All nine declared unsigned comparison narrowing and boundary mutations must fail semantically after a passing unchanged TestNumeric baseline; timeout or build failure cannot count.

Eight actual TLS/RPC histories cover both supported roles, Register/Refresh and parent cancellation/channel closure. Native entered/exited latches, joined caller/server work and 80 successful assertions establish refusal without partial publication, unchanged retry token/directory and released gate ownership. This is not whole-process shutdown or arbitrary runtime interleaving qualification.
